title: Add a compact human-facing packet summary

state.decision_rationale: Deferred until role metadata and cold-open tests show a deterministic summary improves navigation enough to justify duplicated packet tokens. Narrative summaries remain outside the authoritative core.

provenance.source_label: Grok design observation: density versus readability
provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: The format is extremely information-dense. That's a feature for machines, but the index plus outlines plus multi-chunk files make human skimming heavier than a simple tarball plus README. A small human-facing summary header, or a generated table of contents with one-sentence role per file, would help when a person has to open the packet cold.
feedback.normalized_claim: Provide a compact, trustworthy orientation layer for human readers without weakening or duplicating the machine-oriented index.

current_behavior: The packet begins with a one-line guide and machine-oriented metadata, index, global symbols, edges, and omissions.
An optional TOC sidecar lists file IDs, paths, projections, line counts, and symbol counts but does not contain one-sentence roles.
No generated narrative summary is embedded in the packet.

proposal.summary: Evaluate a short human-facing summary or role-oriented TOC that remains clearly derived and non-authoritative.
candidate_changes: Add a deterministic summary block containing counts, major directories, languages, roles, and notable omissions without generated prose.
Extend an optional sidecar with caller-supplied or provenance-backed one-sentence file roles.
Keep narrative model-generated summaries outside the integrity-critical core unless their generator and evidence are declared.
Test whether humans and models orient faster with the summary than with the existing index alone.
non_goals: Do not treat generated prose as repository truth.
Do not duplicate hundreds of index rows in a second embedded table.
Do not increase the default packet materially without measured navigation benefit.

questions: Is the summary intended for humans, models, or both?
Can useful one-sentence roles be derived deterministically, or must they come from the selection manifest?
Should the summary be embedded, a sidecar, or a separate view?
risks: Narrative summaries can be stale, lossy, or confidently wrong.
A second navigation layer may duplicate tokens without changing behavior.
Human-oriented ordering can conflict with deterministic machine ordering.
evidence_needed: Timed cold-open navigation tests with humans and models.
Token-cost measurements for deterministic and narrative summary designs.
Provenance rules for any caller-supplied or generated role descriptions.
